decisive_items: a 1.5 cm intra-articular space-occupying lesion invading the tibial plateau
Gadolinium-enhanced MRI showed enhancement confined to the peripheral rim of the mass, with no satellite lesions identified
was unremarkable on fat-saturated T2 sequences
response.rationale: Solitary intra-articular tibial plateau mass with peripheral rim enhancement and no satellite lesions best fits giant cell tumor; synovial chondromatosis would more typically show multiple intra-articular bodies and high T2 cartilaginous signal.

rejected.why: Lateral knee pain and joint-line tenderness are nonspecific; MRI shows a mass invading bone, not a meniscal tear.
Osteochondroma is a surface/cartilage-capped bony outgrowth with marrow continuity, not an intra-articular rim-enhancing mass invading the tibial plateau.
Synovial chondromatosis usually produces multiple intra-articular chondral bodies/satellite lesions; a solitary invading mass with unremarkable fat-saturated T2 is atypical.
Ganglion cyst would be cystic and T2-hyperintense, not heterogeneous with internal specks and bone invasion.
